cliBody: Word to Markdown is free and open source. Run it as a command-line tool for scripted or batch conversions — the same converter, no browser needed.

faqs.q: How do I convert a Word document to Markdown?
faqs.a: Drag a .docx file onto the page (or click to browse). Word to Markdown converts it in your browser and shows the Markdown instantly — copy it or download a .md file.
Yes. It is completely free and open source — no sign-up, no file limits, and no ads.

faqs.q: Are my documents uploaded to a server?
faqs.a: No. Conversion happens entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Your files never leave your device and are never uploaded, stored, or logged.

faqs.q: How do I convert a Google Doc to Markdown?
faqs.a: In Google Docs, choose File → Download → Microsoft Word (.docx), then drop that .docx into Word to Markdown.

faqs.q: Can I convert a .doc file to Markdown?
faqs.a: Word to Markdown reads modern .docx files. If you have an older .doc file, open it in Word and save it as .docx (File → Save As → Word Document .docx), then drop that .docx in.
Headings, bold, italic, and strikethrough text, superscript and subscript, ordered and nested lists, tables, links, code, and images are converted to clean, GitHub-flavored Markdown.

faqs.q: How is this different from Pandoc?
faqs.a: Pandoc is a powerful command-line converter, but it has to be installed and configured first. Word to Markdown runs instantly in your browser with nothing to install — just drop in a .docx. For scripted or batch jobs, a command-line version is available too.

faqs.q: Can I use this to prepare documents for ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI tools?
faqs.a: Yes. Markdown is a clean, token-efficient format for large language models and RAG pipelines. Converting a Word document to Markdown first gives AI tools well-structured text — headings, lists, and tables — without the noise of binary .docx formatting.
